title: NA-MT223-AnnotationPanel

scope.summary:
GOAL: Add a dedicated ANNOTATION SIDE PANEL to the native shell — a real registered pane (not an ad-hoc egui window) that lists annotations for a chosen scope (current file / current document / whole workspace) with author/state/kind/path filters, sort, jump-to-anchor, inline resolve/reopen/reply, per-state badge counts, and explicit empty/error states. This is the cross-file triage surface for the annotation system: MT-221 renders markers in the code editor and MT-222 in Notes; this panel is the single place an operator reviews every annotation regardless of which file it lives in. Interaction pattern reference: the VS Code Comments panel (the tree-view companion to inline CommentThreads) — a grouped list that mirrors and navigates to the inline threads. The panel REUSES the shared AnnotationThreadWidget (MT-221 annotations/thread_widget.rs) for inline reply/resolve; it does NOT fork a second thread renderer or a second badge component.

EXPECTED DIFF SHAPE: New annotations/panel.rs (AnnotationPanel + filter/sort/scope state) registered as a pane through the REAL shell trio, grounding-verified 2026-07-21: (1) a `pub const ANNOTATION_PANEL_PANE_ID: &str` + `pub fn register_annotation_panel_pane(...)` in pane_registry.rs mirroring register_outline_pane / OUTLINE_PANE_ID = "rich.outline" (pane_registry.rs:483-506); (2) an AnnotationPanelPaneFactory (impl PaneFactory) + ANNOTATION_PANEL_PANE_LABEL const in editor_pane_factories.rs, returning PaneType::Placeholder(label) exactly like the outline/tags/sidebar factories; (3) a mount line in app.rs in the install-side-panels block (near app.rs:3503, where placeholder-keyed factories are inserted via editor_pane_factories::placeholder_pane_type(LABEL)). `pub mod panel;` added to annotations/mod.rs; one integration test file. No NEW PaneType enum variant is added — native side panels use PaneType::Placeholder(String), matching every existing side pane. No backend edits; no legacy React edits; no fork of the shared thread widget.

DETAILED SPEC (pane wiring, structs, filters, flows):
1. PANE REGISTRATION (real mechanism): ANNOTATION_PANEL_PANE_ID = "annotations.panel" (dotted stable key; PaneId = Arc<str>). register_annotation_panel_pane(registry, project_id, scope) inserts PaneRecord::new(pane_id, PaneType::Placeholder(ANNOTATION_PANEL_PANE_LABEL.to_owned()), ...) — insert() preserves any already-assigned AccessKit NodeId on re-registration (pane_registry.rs:247). AnnotationPanelPaneFactory implements PaneFactory { pane_type(), render(ui, ctx: &PaneRenderContext), accesskit_role() => Role::Group } and renders AnnotationPanel. The pane hosts through PaneHostWidget + split_layout.rs like every other side pane; it MUST NOT use raw egui::SidePanel (the shell has no SidePanel-based pane path).
2. SCOPE SELECTOR: `pub enum AnnotationScope { CurrentFile, CurrentDocument, Workspace }`. The panel reads the active editor/document context from interop/interaction_bus.rs InteractionBus (SharedSelection / active-document key, INTERACTION_BUS_KEY = "handshake_interaction_bus"), NEVER by reaching into editor internals. A scope switch re-queries annotations/client.rs (AC list/query route); the panel holds no anchor math.
3. FILTERS: author kind (operator | model), robot_id (options populated from the model-authored annotations actually present), state (open | resolved | orphaned | outdated — the exact MT-221 AnnotationMarkerState vocabulary), kind, and path substring. Filters are PURE over the fetched set (client-side narrowing, no re-query). Each filter control is an AccessKit node with a stable author_id; toggle controls use Role::CheckBox (accesskit 0.21.1 has NO Role::ToggleButton — see code_editor/panel.rs:231), and any search/filter text field uses Role::SearchInput (no Role::SearchBox in 0.21.1).
4. SORT: by path, by state, by author kind, by updated_at; sort is a pure reordering of the filtered set.
5. ROW RENDERING: each row shows the provenance badge (operator vs model — the SAME badge component MT-221 uses; model badge shows robot_id + session id), a one-line head preview, the path + anchor location, and the state chip. Row AccessKit id: annotation_panel_row_{annotation_id}. Clicking/activating a row expands the shared AnnotationThreadWidget inline (read + interact per MT-221; the create/update mutations land in MT-224).
6. JUMP-TO-ANCHOR: a per-row jump control opens the target file/document, scrolls to the MT-221/MT-222 rendered placement, and briefly FLASHES that marker. Navigation goes through the real seam — navigation_bus.rs NavigationTarget + ShellNavigator (HandshakeApp::open_navigator_tab) and/or InteractionBus — NOT a bespoke opener. Jump moves focus ONLY when the operator activated it (HBR-QUIET-003): operator activation intentionally moves focus to the opened editor; a passive list refresh or badge update NEVER moves focus or raises a window.
7. INLINE RESOLVE / REOPEN / REPLY: rendered via the shared thread widget; the panel exposes the controls and calls the client seam. The actual mutation implementation (AC MT-205 tools) is MT-224 — this MT wires the controls and the read path only.
8. BADGE COUNTS: a header shows counts per state (open/resolved/orphaned/outdated) and per author kind for the current scope+filter. Counts are DERIVED FROM THE FETCHED BACKEND SET for the scope, never from a cached UI number or the rendered/paginated subset (SOT discipline: panel count must equal the backend set for the scope).
9. EMPTY + ERROR STATES: an explicit 'No annotations in {scope}' empty state and a DISTINCT error state (client/route failure) with a retry affordance — never a blank pane, never a silent failure.

STEP-BY-STEP:
1. Read pane_registry.rs (PaneId/PaneType/PaneRecord/PaneRegistry/trait PaneFactory/PaneRenderContext/PaneHostWidget, register_outline_pane pattern :483-506), editor_pane_factories.rs (label consts :2225-2235 + placeholder_pane_type + install label consts), app.rs (build_default_factories :3074, install side-panels block :3503+), interop/interaction_bus.rs (SharedSelection/active document), navigation_bus.rs (NavigationTarget, ShellNavigator, NavError), annotations/client.rs + thread_widget.rs (MT-221 seams), manual_pane.rs + manual_content_editors.rs (manual entry mechanism).
2. Add ANNOTATION_PANEL_PANE_ID + register_annotation_panel_pane to pane_registry.rs; AnnotationPanelPaneFactory + ANNOTATION_PANEL_PANE_LABEL to editor_pane_factories.rs; mount in app.rs.
3. Build AnnotationPanel: scope selector, filter + sort state, row list reusing the shared thread widget + shared badge component.
4. Wire jump-to-anchor through navigation_bus/InteractionBus with the flash effect and the operator-only focus-move rule.
5. Add badge counts, empty/error states, AccessKit ids; add the manual topic; write the integration test and capture Argus evidence for every panel surface and state.
forbidden_paths: app/src/** (legacy React notes editor is scheduled for REMOVAL by MT-261..264 — never extend it)
src/backend/** (annotation core is AC MT-201..209; consume via routes only)
src/frontend/handshake_native/src/annotations/thread_widget.rs (REUSE the shared widget; do not fork or add a panel-only thread renderer)
acceptance_criteria: A new annotation side pane is registered through the real shell trio: ANNOTATION_PANEL_PANE_ID + register_annotation_panel_pane in pane_registry.rs, AnnotationPanelPaneFactory + ANNOTATION_PANEL_PANE_LABEL in editor_pane_factories.rs, and a mount in app.rs install-side-panels; it hosts via PaneHostWidget/split_layout with PaneType::Placeholder (no new PaneType variant, no raw egui::SidePanel).

The panel lists annotations for AnnotationScope { CurrentFile, CurrentDocument, Workspace }, reading active context from InteractionBus (no reaching into editor internals); switching scope re-queries the client seam.

Filters (author kind operator|model, robot_id, state open|resolved|orphaned|outdated, kind, path) and sort (path/state/author/updated_at) narrow purely over the fetched set; toggle controls use Role::CheckBox and any filter text field uses Role::SearchInput (accesskit 0.21.1 constraints honored).

Each row shows the SAME provenance badge component as MT-221 (operator vs model; model badge shows robot_id + session id), a head preview, path/anchor, and state chip; row AccessKit id is annotation_panel_row_{annotation_id}; activating a row expands the SHARED AnnotationThreadWidget inline.

Jump-to-anchor opens the target file/document via navigation_bus/ShellNavigator/InteractionBus, scrolls to the MT-221/MT-222 placement, and flashes the marker; focus moves ONLY on operator activation, never on passive refresh (HBR-QUIET-003).
Badge counts per state and per author kind are derived from the fetched backend set for the scope (equal to the backend set, not the rendered/paginated subset) — SOT-verified in a test.
Explicit empty state ('No annotations in {scope}') and a distinct error state with retry exist; the pane is never blank and never fails silently.
annotations/client.rs additions (if any) contain no anchor/reanchor math (grep-provable); the panel reuses thread_widget.rs unchanged (no fork).
UserManual updated in the same change: the Annotations panel — scope, filters, sort, jump-to-anchor, resolve/reopen/reply, badge counts, empty/error states.
proof_targets: Argus evidence: argus.inspect (AccessKit tree) + argus.screenshot of (a) panel with mixed operator+model rows, (b) each filter/sort applied, (c) all four state badge counts, (d) an expanded shared thread widget in-panel, (e) empty state, (f) error+retry state — stored under the external HANDSHAKE_ARTIFACTS_ROOT
code_surfaces: src/frontend/handshake_native/src/annotations/client.rs (list/query consumption for the panel scope; no anchor math)
expected_tests: unit: filter predicate narrows the fetched set correctly for each filter axis (author kind, robot_id, state, kind, path)
unit: sort orders by path/state/author/updated_at deterministically
unit: badge counts equal the fetched backend set per state and author kind (SOT: not the rendered subset)
integration: scope switch (CurrentFile -> CurrentDocument -> Workspace) re-queries the client seam and updates the list
integration: pane registers through the trio and is discoverable in the PaneRegistry with PaneType::Placeholder(ANNOTATION_PANEL_PANE_LABEL)
integration: activating a row expands the shared AnnotationThreadWidget (same struct as MT-221) with correct AccessKit ids
negative: empty scope renders the empty state; a client error renders the error+retry state (never blank)
implementation_notes: Verified grounding 2026-07-21 (wtc-native-editors-v1): the shell is a single HandshakeApp in app.rs (no shell.rs); side panels register via the pane_registry.rs trio (PaneId=Arc<str>, enum PaneType with Placeholder(String), PaneRecord, PaneRegistry, trait PaneFactory, PaneRenderContext, PaneHostWidget) mounted in app.rs (build_default_factories :3074, install side-panels :3503+ using editor_pane_factories::placeholder_pane_type). Copy the register_outline_pane / OUTLINE_PANE_ID = "rich.outline" pattern (pane_registry.rs:483-506) exactly.

accesskit is transitively pinned 0.21.1 (eframe 0.33 accesskit feature): no Role::ToggleButton (use Role::CheckBox), no Role::SearchBox (use Role::SearchInput), no Role::TextCursor — see the documented constraints in code_editor/panel.rs:150-236. Role::Group/Label/Button/ScrollView exist.

Active-context reads go through interop/interaction_bus.rs InteractionBus (Arc<Mutex<InteractionBus>> in ctx.data, key "handshake_interaction_bus", interaction_bus_id()); navigation/jump goes through navigation_bus.rs NavigationTarget + ShellNavigator (HandshakeApp::open_navigator_tab). Do NOT open documents by any bespoke path.

Reuse the shared AnnotationThreadWidget and the operator/model badge from annotations/thread_widget.rs unchanged; adding authoring buttons is MT-224's job (this MT renders read + exposes control intents only).

Manual: add a ManualTopic to editors_manual_section() in manual_content_editors.rs; every documented author_id must be a live registered id (an id-audit test cross-checks this) — use annotation_panel_row_{annotation_id}, the panel container id, and the filter control ids.

Design basis (cite in code docs): VS Code Comments panel (tree-view companion to inline CommentThreads) as the list/triage pattern; the panel mirrors, never replaces, the inline threads of MT-221/MT-222.

Cross-family seams (reference only, not authored here): MT-221 markers + shared widget + strip + client seam, MT-222 rich placements the jump lands on, MT-224 authoring mutations, MT-225 live arrival badge increment + quarantine section, AC MT-203/207 list/query routes, MM MT-104 quarantine flag (surfaced by MT-225).

surfaces: filter controls (author kind, robot_id, state, kind, path)
annotation row list with provenance badges + state chips

target_entries: Annotations panel: scope (current file/document/workspace), filters, sort, jump-to-anchor, inline resolve/reopen/reply, badge counts, empty/error states

hbr_int_009_tier_obligations.reason: The panel emits no new business events; annotation lifecycle FR events are the AC/MT-161 seam and mutations are MT-224.

Scope/filter state, fetched-vs-rendered counts, and jump-target resolution are exposed as structured state readable by the visual_debugger surface for no-context diagnosis of a wrong count or a failed jump.
Pure render/list surface; no long-running child process to liveness-track.

risk_if_missed: There is no cross-file review surface for annotations: operators can only find model feedback by opening each file and hunting gutter/margin markers, orphaned and file-level annotations (which never render at a body line) have no home, and MT-225 has no panel to increment or quarantine section to fill.

risks: RISK-1: Count lie — the header badge counts reflect only the loaded/filtered/paginated rows, not the backend set for the scope, so an operator believes review is complete when unshown annotations remain (SOT violation).

RISK-2: Focus theft on refresh — a passive list refresh, badge increment, or scope repopulate steals keyboard focus or raises the pane while the operator is typing in an editor (HBR-QUIET-003 regression).

RISK-3: Provenance divergence — the panel renders its own row badge instead of the shared MT-221 component, so operator vs model distinction (or robot_id/session display) drifts between the panel and the inline threads.

RISK-4: Widget/pane fork — the panel builds a private thread renderer or uses raw egui::SidePanel instead of the shared widget and the real pane registry, breaking Argus addressing and the shell layout contract.
RISK-5: Orphaned/file-level invisibility — annotations with no body-line placement (orphaned or rangeless) are dropped from the list, leaving them with no surface anywhere.
minimum_controls: CTRL-1 (RISK-1): Counts computed from the fetched backend set for the scope; a test asserts count == backend set size, distinct from the rendered-row count; error/partial-fetch states never report a full count.

CTRL-2 (RISK-2): Focus moves only on explicit operator activation (row/jump); passive refresh never calls request_focus or window raise; a QUIET test asserts no focus change on a background repopulate.
CTRL-3 (RISK-3): Panel rows import the shared operator/model badge from thread_widget.rs; a test asserts the same badge kind + robot_id/session fields as the inline widget.
CTRL-4 (RISK-4): Grep proof — no egui::SidePanel and no second ThreadWidget struct in panel.rs; the pane is discoverable in the PaneRegistry via the trio; PaneFactory/PaneHostWidget path used.

CTRL-5 (RISK-5): Workspace scope includes orphaned and file-level annotations with an explicit location label ('unanchored' / 'file-level'); a test asserts they appear in the panel even when they render nowhere in the editors.
